newsitem.title: UK: UK gilts close off lows, dicing with key support.
newsitem.headline: UK gilts close off lows, dicing with key support.

text.p: UK gilts closed just above the day's lows but still dicing with key support levels after earlier shrugging off M4 money supply data.

"The market's been in terminal decline today with damage being done by various unnamed U.S. houses," one senior trader said. "We have gone down with Germany." Earlier the market was unimpressed with figures showing the M4 money supply had expanded by less than expected. Provisional figures for M4 money supply showed a 10.4 percent year-on-year increase in April compared to the 11.3 percent expected.
"The market has singularly failed to respond to figures, last week and this week," the trader said.
And with June gilts hovering above the key 112-28 level, traders said the market could be in for a rough ride if it dipped any lower.
Having soared after finance minister Gordon Brown granted the Bank of England operational independence two weeks ago, gilts slipped back to 112-28 on May 8 before climbing higher.
"Below 112-28 there is really no support until you get down to 111-12. This one could get very nasty," another trader said.
Traders have cited the 112-28 level as a key support level which, if breached could spark a large bout of selling.

The market would be looking to Thursday's retail sales figures for encouragement but the signs were that consumer spending was on the up. "The pace of spending on the high street is looking increasingly robust as consumer sentiment continues to improve," said Dharshini David, UK economist at HSBC Markets.
But traders said the figures would have to be flat to help the market move higher.

The auction by the Bank of England of 1.5 billion sterling of 8.0 percent gilts due 2021 should be digested by the market, traders said, with good institutional demand. "The gilt auction should not be a problem. It's probably going to be well covered by the long-term institutions, the pension funds and insurance companies," the trader said.
